items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: I figured Gene Orloff was going to be the concertmaster

ctx.x: Well the musical description that you’ve written was very specific. Was it written — did you have this whole scenario in mind when you started, even down to describing the muted sound of Nick Travis — I believe that’s the trumpet player’s name?

Yeah. Well both he and Art played in the mutes, there were two different mutes and each one traded off as a matter of fact. But oh yeah, I had all that, I knew who I was going to have. I knew I was going to have Nick, and I mentioned them. Nick, Art, Brookmeyer was going to be a soloist, Al Cohn was and Phil Woods and Gene Quill, who were the two great alto players. They were alter-egos for each other. And so I knew they would be there. Eddie Costa, an incredible piano player — unfortunately he ended his life too…
Well I’m glad you mention that, I just wanted to —
